text: There is generally no coverage under a CGL policy because such claims flow from intentional acts by the employer or ERISA fiduciary, not accidental “occurrences.” In addition, most ERISA claims do not seek damages for “bodily injury” within the meaning of the policy (see ¶ 3:356). A special form of insurance coverage (Employee Benefits Liability or EBL coverage) is now available to cover such claims. See ¶ 3:280 ff. 7. [3:506] Contract Claims: Most breach of contract claims are not covered under a CGL policy because they do not involve “bodily injury” or an accidental “occurrence” (see ¶ 3:292 ff.) or because another policy limitation applies. [See B & E Convalescent Ctr. v. State Comp. Ins. Fund (1992) 8 CA4th 78, 85, 9 CR2d 894, 898, fn. 5—contract claim for wrongful termination based on breach of implied covenant not within scope of liability coverage because termination not an “accident” (¶ 3:357); Ray v. Valley Forge Ins.
